MINUTES

  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING

  NOVEMBER 7, 2016

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A Regular Meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by CHAIR
SCHACHTER.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

CHAIR SCHACHTER led the assembly in the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.

3.  ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Zigrang, Scott, Yoo, Medawar, Carman, Chair Schachter
Commissioners Absent:  Thomas
Staff Present:  Planning Director Wahba, Associate Planner Thom

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO,

  TO APPROVE THE MINUTES OF THE REGULAR PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING OF OCTOBER 3, 2016.

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

None.

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

None.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 28-16; APPLICANT: Mr. Adam Rick; LOCATION: 44
  Dapplegray Lane; A Neighborhood Compatibility Determination to construct a pool/spa,
  pool house and other rear yard improvements. A Grading application is required to fill in
  a slope.

Associate Planner Thom summarized the staff report and asked if the Planning Commission
had any questions.

In response to a question from COMMISSIONER SCOTT, Associate Planner Thom said that
the Homeowners Association had signed off on the project.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT had concern that the pool house would be nearer than 35’ from
neighboring horsekeeping facilities and that if the pool house became habitable it would render
the nearby barns illegal. After some discussion Director Wahba stated that at a later time if
someone wanted to make the pool house into a second dwelling unit, it would not qualify
because of the setback.

CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER asked if there was anyone in the audience that wished to speak on
the project.

Planning Commission Minutes  1
November 7, 2016
 Mr. Alan McGregor (Landscape Architect, Huntington Beach, CA) came forward and said that
the purpose of the pool house was to accommodate the kids because the bathroom in the home
was so remote from the pool that they needed to put one closer.

By invitation of CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER, Mr. Adam Rick (Applicant) came forward and stated
that it was not their intent to rent the structure out, and that it was just a pool house.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked whether the pool house could be moved a little further from
the property lines and in response, Mr. McGregor stated that because of the covered
patio/outdoor dining area the pool house could not be moved.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that he would like to see it further from the property line where
the barn was the closest to it.

In response to a question from COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR, Associate Planner Thom stated
that they had not received any objections to the project from any neighbors.

COMMISSIONERS MEDAWAR and ZIGRANG stated that they were in favor of the project.

COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated that her only concern was that there would be lots of noise
going to adjacent neighbors that comes from pool activity and would like to see more of a buffer.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG,

  TO APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 28-16 WITH THE CONDITIONS THAT
  IT NOT BE USED AS A SECOND DWELLING UNIT, AND CANNOT BE RENTED OR
  OCCUPIED FOR SLEEPING PURPOSES, AND ONLY BE USED AS A POOL HOUSE,
  AND THAT THE HOMEOWNERS ASSOCIATION GIVE APPROVAL FOR TRAIL
  ACCESS DURING GRADING.

AYES:  Zigrang, Scott, Yoo, Carman, Medawar, Chair Schachter
NOES:
ABSTAIN:
ABSENT:  Thomas

Planning Director Wahba explained the 20-day appeal period for item 7-A.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 31-16; APPLICANT:  Mr. Thomas Fitzpatrick;
  LOCATION: 25851 Hawthorne Blvd.; A Special Use Permit for a request to allow 12
  horses on the property.

Associate Planner Thom summarized the staff report and stated that Commission will find two
emails on the dais that staff received too late to include in the staff report: from Alex Costa (#59
Hidden Valley Road, RHE, against the project) and Herbert Carlborn (#4432 Via Pavion, PVE,
in favor of the project). Planning Director Wahba spoke further (per written material) and told
the Planning Commission that they need to provide the applicant and staff with direction in
terms of how they would move forward with the project.

In response to a question from CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER, Planning Director Wahba stated that
portions of the trails were not recorded easements, but that they have been used for many
years and they eventually need to do a study to show what easements are in place, which are
not, and what easements could be proposed to maintain some level of public access through
the property.

In response to another question from CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER, Planning Director Wahba
clarified the location and details of the water monitoring site, and added that due to the location
of the property it was prone to flooding, and one of the issues the City had was to minimize the
manure from going into the monitoring station there.

In response to another question from CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER regarding whether the City had
exercised any control over this property and whether any of the structures were built without
permits, Planning Director Wahba stated that they were unable to find permit records although
pipe corrals could be exempt from requiring a building permit depending upon how they were
built but that technically anything larger than 120 square feet of projected roof area requires a
building permit. He added that these structures had been there for a very long time, and that
there were other buildings there on the site that have been removed due to code enforcement

Planning Commission Minutes  2
November 7, 2016
 efforts through the years.

COMMISSIONER YOO asked if there appeared to be an intent that there would be commercial
use in the area, to which Planning Director Wahba explained that the intent was just for family
use and not for commercial.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that he visited the site that afternoon and there was no
evidence of any commercial use taking place there.

COMMISSIONER YOO asked in terms of the phosphorous content issue, whether it was a
direct result of this property. Planning Director Wahba stated that there were a number of other
horse properties that were contributing to the drainage ravine, but that obviously increasing the
number of horses to 12 would be something that needs to be looked at. The solution would
probably be some sort of a berm that would be put up to protect the stream so that the manure
and urine would be kept on the property and in a rain event would not be washing into that area.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that he specifically walked the area up both of the ravines and
he could not identify any active horse uses other than P.V. Stables. Planning Director Wahba
stated that there are horsekeeping facilities from Hidden Valley and Sugarhill that drain into that
area, and that that trail was used quite a bit.

CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER asked whether it was the proposal to grandfather-in the existing
structures and Planning Director Wahba answered that that applicant wished to use what was
already there at this time and that it could house 12 horses.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

There being no objection, CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER so ordered.

Dirk Ryke (Architect, Redondo Beach), stated that they were not there to discuss the caretaker
home because it would be a big undertaking due to there being a large number of adjacent
neighbors to both the property and to the easements. The caretaker home would be a long-
range project and they aren’t even sure if the project would be feasible. Mr. Fitzpatrick was only
making a request to add eight horses (making a total of 12) to the property at this time while he
still has the time to enjoy his family. He stated that they could accommodate 12 horses easily
without adding any kind of structure to it.

Chris Fitzpatrick (with Applicant), told the Commission how he had grown up with horses and
now kept three at the Empty Saddle Club, but that he would like to keep them on the family
property, along with his brothers’ horses, and nieces horses, and that equestrian activities were
something that the entire family enjoyed doing together.

CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER asked Mr. Fitzpatrick whether it was ever used for commercial uses
to which he replied that it was, but that his father never made any money from it and it was just
to help the other people.

Kevin Fitzpatrick (with Applicant) stated that in the past the manure may have been a problem,
but that now the manure goes into the green waste container every day and is picked up by a
service every Friday.

Tracy Fitzpatrick (wife of Kevin Fitzpatrick), says that she goes on the property 2-3 times daily
and her daughter rides. She said there is a ton of people coming through the property walking
their dogs, horses, kids, boy and girl scouts on nature hikes, and their Grandfather, Mr. Thomas
Fitzpatrick, wanted to keep the property open and not close anything off. In the past the
property was dilapidated but was very nice now and is clean, with children riding in the arena.
They have many family get-togethers there. She added that there were no commercial trail
rides originating from their property.

Katherine Arafit, (4428 Via Pavion, PVE), lives directly above the property. She has two small
children that run down the canyon every day to play and they enjoy it very much.

Janine Slane (4429 Via Pavion, PVE), lives directly adjacent to Howlett Park and the facility.
She stated that there is horse manure all over the place and even on the street and when she
walks her dog it is everywhere, and she is overwhelmed with the stench of the horses. She
feels that it disturbs the tranquility of her home She feels that 12 horses are too many and that
it isn’t fair. Also, she is afraid that it will turn into a business. She added that horses attract rats,
that attract cats, which in turn attract coyotes.

Planning Commission Minutes  3
November 7, 2016
 Herb Carlbom, (4432 Via Pavion, PVE) said that he has no problem with the property and it is
kept very clean, and there is no smell.

Jeannie Slane returned to the dais and added that she felt that since RHE is a small city, if
someone wanted 12 horses they should move to Colorado or Montana.

Katherine Arafit returned to the dais and said that the manure found on the street is not from the
Fitzpatrick’s horses but is from the barn up the street (PV Stables in PVE) from the horses that
she sees coming up their street all the time. She added that she has never smelled anything
coming from the property and they live right next to it.

Tom Fitzpatrick (Applicant, 4111 Paseo de las Tortugas, Torrance) gave a history of the
property and how he came to own it. He passed out a copy of his family tree showing that he
had many grandkids and great grandkids, and that he promised them that they could all have a
horse. They should not be held to the residential standard of a four horse maximum because it
is not a residential lot.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

There being no objection, CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER so ordered.

COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that he is a Board Member of the Empty Saddle Club as are
two of the Fitzpatricks, but that he can be objective. He said the property looks better than it did
12 years ago, and the family was going in the right direction as far as being good neighbors. He
was in favor of allowing them to up the number of horses considering the size of the property
and that the corrals were already there, and that eight more horses would not be as impactful as
it sounds.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that although he is not a horse person, when he visited
the site it was evident that there was plenty of room for 12 horses.

CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER stated that before any decisions are made, he would like to get a
handle on the following: easement rights, who has access to the property, and who is coming
through the property. He asked whether there were formally dedicated easements, to which
Planning Director Wahba replied that there were none, but that they could work with the
applicant and get that information.

In response to a question from COMMISSIONER YOO, Planning Director Wahba stated that he
would have to check to see whether the facility would require a public health permit from L.A.
County.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR said that he felt that there was no reason to hold back from
allowing more horses and that other issues could be looked at separately.

COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated that part of her interest is the environmental impact on the
canyon and seeing what kind of mitigation measures can be done to limit the potential leaching
of the waste, to see if it is protected from washout, drainage issues and looking for innovative
measures to reduce the smells.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that he didn’t think that there is enough information on the
water quality issue and he believed that RHE is going to bear some financial and performance
responsibility to the State water quality people in terms of what is disposed at the storm catch
areas down into Machado Lake so he wanted to know more how much difference eight more
horses would make in that regard. He also wanted to see if there could be a County Health
person that could come by and do a pre-inspection of the facility as a condition of keeping 12
horses onsite before the horses are brought onsite. He also wanted to prohibit any renting of
stalls.

Planning Director Wahba confirmed for CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER that all the cities are being
surcharged for pollution going down into Machado Lake, and that some of this is a direct result
of horses.

COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated her concerns that before a berm or grading on the property
commence that there be a study how rain would affect it.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG,

Planning Commission Minutes  4
November 7, 2016
   TO CONTINUE THE PUBLIC HEARING TO A DATE UNCERTAIN TO ALLOW THE
  APPLICANT TIME TO ADDRESS THE ISSUES AS SUMMARIZED IN THE STAFF
  REPORT AND DIRECTION SUGGESTED BY THE COMMISSION.

AYES:  Zigrang, Scott, Yoo, Carman, Medawar, Chair Schachter
NOES:
ABSTAIN:
ABSENT:  Thomas

9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

COMMISSIONER SCOTT mentioned that directly in front of the old parking lot of the Country
Club, the horsetrail behind the fence is blocked by landscaping and boulders.

In response to a question from COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG, Planning Director Wahba updated
the Commission on status of the Carriage Drive project that was before the Commissioners
recently.

In response from a question from COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR, Planning Director Wahba
stated that the Anastasi Development at 627 Deep Valley Drive is moving forward, with the Final
Map going to Council for approval in January or February.

10.  DIRECTOR’S ITEMS

Planning Director Wahba stated that the next Planning Commission meeting would be on
December 5th, the first Monday in December. He added that the Holiday Parade would take
place December 3rd, and the Annual Holiday Party at the Norris Pavilion will take place on
December 8th.

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES (10/17/16)

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS (10/10/16)

  C.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS (10/25/16)

COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, and COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG seconded,

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE ITEMS 11A THROUGH 11C.

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

12.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:49 p.m. CHAIR SCHACHTER adjourned the Planning Commission meeting to December
5, 2016, at 7:00 p.m.
